ctx.x: It was amazing to black musicians from America to find how much specialist interest some Europeans were taking in our music. At that time, the average American didn't know Count Basie from Duke Ellington. Even when Duke Ellington came over here in the 30's, people knew all about him. They wanted to know who was the trumpet player and who was the saxophone player - their interest and enthusiasm was so high they wanted to know the whole history of the band! In America, nobody could care less. You'd see it on the…

I was invited to visit the club which was on rue Mansart not far from Boudons. There I met the secretary of the club who was a fellow named Charles Delaunay and the treasurer whose name was Pierre Nourry. The club was on the ground floor and when I walked into the reception room, I saw the names of Coleman Hawkins, Louis Armstrong, and all the known jazz men of the time, written on the wall. The club was also a meeting place for jazz lovers, who were members of the club and French jazz musicians who would come…

It was about this time that I began to get interested in studying harmony. My first attempts were not too successful. When I was in New York, just before leaving France, I'd been taking harmony lessons
